newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Alliance vows not to give up on Forestry Corp.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Alliance vows not to give up on Forestry Corp.

text.p: Left-wing Alliance Party leader Jim Anderton said on Monday his party would not give up in its bid to reverse the sale of Forestry Corp.
The party's nationwide petition aimed at forcing a referendum on the sale was rejected last week because it fell more than 40,000 signatures short.
Emerging for a lunch adjournment from a meeting with the centre-left Labour Party on Monday, Anderton was asked by reporters if his party would give up on the Forestry Corp issue.
"Absolutely not. We will immediately make plans in caucus to get the rest of the signatures we need," he replied.
Anderton said the party had a further 8,000 signatures that were not included in the original petition.
There is a two-month deadline allowed by legislation for petitions to be re-presented.

The petition was circulated during the sale of Forestry Corp and signatures continued to be gathered even after the former state-owned corporation was sold in September for $2 billion to a consortium led by Fletcher Challenge.
By law, petitions must have the signatures of at least 10 percent of registered electors at the time the petition is presented in order to force a national referendum on the relevant issue.

That would have required 240,429 legitimate signatures for the forestry petition to be accepted by parliament. When it was presented last month, the Alliance claimed it had 246,466 signatures, but after checks it was revealed that only about 197,000 were legitimate.

Citizens-initiated referenda are not binding on the government, so even if the Alliance does find the necessary signatures to force a referendum, the government can ignore the result. -- Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
